response.sql: WITH pair_avg AS (SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) AS mean_avg FROM pair_avg), excess AS (SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_feerate, p.avg_feerate - o.mean_avg AS excess FROM pair_avg p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_feerate > o.mean_avg), ranked AS (SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY acctscope ORDER BY excess DESC) AS rank_in_scope FROM excess) SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, rank_in_scope FROM ranked WHERE rank_in_scope <= 3 ORDER BY acctscope, rank_in_scope

assumptions.assumption: The mean of pair averages is a single global mean over all (orderslink, acctscope) pairs, not a per-scope mean. Pairs whose feerate values are all NULL have a NULL average, so they are left out of that mean and cannot pass the strictly-above filter.
Ties in excess within a scope are broken arbitrarily by ROW_NUMBER, so each scope returns at most 3 rows.

alternatives.interpretation: Ties in excess share a rank (RANK), so a scope can return more than 3 pairs if they tie at rank 3.
